x: Bill Sutton was seen at the Hall recently. Jim Heathfield, another one at Hamburg, previously at Bruges.
How many other Belgravians have saved the Army's petrol at the expense of their leather! Jim Heathfield, with the B.A.O.R., met Sid. Jones in Germany, and they had a long chat together.
We had a club 220 yards handicap event on the same programme and this was won by Les Christmas (18), with Jim Heathfield (14), on leave from the B.A.O.R., second and Charlie Jones (20) third.

Jim Heathfield was second in the 440 and Terry Bateman won the high jump. Tea and sandwiches were provided afterwards by our hosts, prominent among whom were our old friends Syd Jarlett and Bill Speaight..

Jim Heathfield was third in the 440, John Cope won the 880 in 2 mins. 1.6 secs., while Bill Lucas won the mile in 4 mins. 30.2 secs. Charlie Smart, home on leave from Germany, turned out in the 2 miles and clocked 9 mins. 45 secs. to win a good race with Ted Stimpson second.
Ches Walker won the 880 and Bob Taylor filled fourth place to score a point for us, but in the 440 yards Herne Hill had the first three home with Jim Heathfield first of our runners.

Odde was second in the 440, with Jim Heathfield third. Reg Bolam was third in the mile, with Bob Taylor fourth and Basil Walden was second to Pugh, of S.L.H., in the 220, with Des Mullen in third place.
Cope was not defending his 440 Senior title and Jim Heathfield proved the new champion with I.
The senior match saw " Ginger " Holtum win the 100, with " Paddy " Mullen second in the 220, while Jim Heathfield was third in the 440 yards.

Jim Heathfield was second in the 440, with Alan Bishop and his brother, Len, being second and third in the half-mile. Bob Taylor was second in the 1 mile, with Reg Bolam in fourth place, and Len Adams was second in the 2 miles run, with George Durrant in third place.
In the senior medley race we had John Bromley doing the half-mile leg, with Jim Heathfield the 440, and Alan Picton and Alan Bishop, both last-minute substitutes, the two 220's.

Jim Heathfield also competed, but our quarter men are not yet up to this standard of competition. In the 880 we had both Jack Brown and John Bromley qualify for the final and, although Bromley took the lead with 220 yards to go, with Jack on his heels, they had to give best down the straight, to eve…

…relay, in which the team was : Lowers, Sexton, Craft and Holtum, and the medley relay, in which we had Geoff Osmint and Jim Heathfield doing the two half-laps with Badiali finishing up over the final one lap to win a good race from the North representative.…
Bill made amends, however, by winning the three miles in easy fashion, and Jim Heathfield ran a fine race to win the 440 yards, with Alan Picton gaining third place in the 220 final.
Jim Heathfield was second in the 880, and Reg Bolam was third in the one mile, but the final match points were : Dorking St. Paul's A.C., 67; Belgrave H., 28; Horsham Blue Star H., 12.

The senior 440 saw Ian Badiali gain a second title in quite fast time, and Jim Heathfield was a good second with Bob Wolton a plucky third. Don Maclean won the junior mile, as expected, and from the way he went off he seemed quite determined to make sure that Geoff Goode had no reserves of speed left.
Ian Badiali won the 440 yards, with Jim Heathfield second, and Dicky Bartlett was second in the 220, while Bill Lucas was first home in the 2 miles run, with Les Stokell second.

The 440 yards saw Jim Heathfield and "Jock" Cameron running for us and "Jock" duly won his heat and so qualified for the final. Jim showed he was short of training and could not make it but in the final Cameron ran well to finish 2nd to Duffy, of the Polytechnic H.
Jim Heathfield was second, a position he usually occupies in Club championship races over this distance, and Alan Bishop was third. Peter Casselton retained his 440 junior title with J.
Jim Heathfield won the 440 senior with Alan Bishop second and J.

The finals of these so-called London Championships were held at Battersea Park on 6th September, and we had quite a number of our lads who had qualified in the various area races. Jim Heathfield was 2nd in the N.E. London 440 yds. on July 19th, while in the S.W.

Gordon was 3rd, with Ron Morrell 5th in the Senior 100 and John Burr and Archie Bedford were 3rd and 4th in the 1 mile, which was won in 4 mins. 25 secs. by Brian Hewson, of Mitcham. Our team of Jim Heathfield, D. Butler, Ivan Mayers and Bob Wolton won the 1 mile medley relay, beating Mitcham, with Hercules third.
Ray Tooby won the 660 yards Senior, with Jim Heathfield in 2nd place, and Bob Wolton won the Senior 300 yards, with Ron Morrell in 4th place.

We also won the 1 miles medley relay, with Jim Heathfield, Bob Wolton, Ron Morrell and Ivan Mayers. In the Junior match we again triumphed, with 29 pts., with Shaftesbury H., 22 ; and Ealing and Maidenhead, 8 each.
Dicky also won the 440 yds., beating Ian Badiali, and Jim Heathfield was 3rd in the 880, with Don Maclean 2nd in the 1 mile in 4 mins. 26.9 secs.
Basil Walden, Pete Cornish and Alan Law all qualified for the 100 yds. final, but could not get placed in the first three, and Jim Heathfield also reached the 440 final.
Daniels, was 2nd in the 440 yds. and Jim Heathfield ran well to win the 880 in 2 mins. 4 secs. In the 2 miles team race we had Bill Lucas, Stan Davies, and I.

A poor showing, some might say, but not one entirely of our own making, as Jim Heathfield was also away on holiday,. and it must be remembered that quite a number of our lads have Middlesex qualifications and so cannot run for us in Surrey County events.

In the 1 mile medley relay our team of Jim Heathfield, Bob Wolton, Merrett and Key finished 4th, and so scored three points. It was in the field events that we scored best and our men are to be congratulated on their fine showing.

In the 440 yds. we saw Dicky Bartlett beat Bob Taylor, with Jim Heathfield in third place. The " big " event of the meeting was the Club 3 mile track championship, and the holder, Jack Brown, retained his title in 14 mins. 31.4 secs.

The 4 x 440 yds. saw only six teams competing and so this event was run as a final and we finished 5th, and at least our team of Bob Wolton, Jim Heathfield, Bob Taylor and " Jock " Cameron had the satisfaction of beating the Midland champions, Coventry Godiva H.
Bob Taylor won the 880 yds. in 1 min. 58.3 secs., which is a new championship record, and Len Bishop was second, with Jim Heathfield in third place.

We also had first two in the 880 yds., and Jim Heathfield just "pipped" Bob Wolton for 1st place. Our team of Ian Badiali, Ron Morrell, Bob Wolton and " Jock " Cameron also won the 1 mile scratch relay in the good time of 3 mins. 36.8 secs.

Cornish gained another 3rd place in the 440 yards and Jim Heathfield was second in the 880 yards. Jim Masters ran well in the three miles but did not have sufficient speed at the finish and finished 2nd to J.
No one really shone at Ealing though it was a revelation to see Jimmy Heathfield turning out in the 100, 220 and Relay while Mike Lyons managed a 10.3 in his heat of the 100.

The remainder of the meeting should have been taken up by Club handicaps, but owing to lack of support for certain events, they were reduced to the 440 yards and two miles walk. In the 440 yards J. Heathfield finished 1st in 50.5s. with G.
The quarter saw Jan Stephens 2nd and Jim Heathfield, having his first run this season, third. Brian Hallowell won the 880 yards with George Davidson 3rd.

Considering that a field of 130 faced the starter, our lads performed extremely well. A special word of praise to Jim Heathfield, a newcomer to this distance on the roads who covered the course in 55m.55secs.
Colin, Eric and Len were firmly dug in at 8th, 9th and 15th respectively and Jim Heathfield, confounding everyone, looked very comfortable in 28th place.

Although still very husky from a heavy cold, Shippen was about the 100 mark with Len Bishop, Eddie Short and Jim Heathfield further back. And so it was, our lads hung on grimly to their early gains and ran out a good third with Jack Brown, a little disappointed perhaps, our first man home.

The brothers Bishop (Alan and Eric) indulged in some good pack running with Jim Heathfield and Bob Glover in attendance. The final reckoning gave Herne Hill a win by 95 pts. to 115 in the senior and 18 to 20 in the junior.
Eddie Short ran well to take sixth place and that "little potterer" Joe Dooley followed close on his heels with Jim Heathfield, only a few yards behind.

Henry Martin produced a promising early season effort in the quarter when running a close second to Woodland of Hercules(52.0) and, although only placed fifth, it was good to see Jim Heathfield running quarters once more after his third retirement from the event!
Derek Crookes is rapidly becoming a junior Jim Heathfield. Although Club 100 yards Junior Champion, he recently ran well in a road race of almost 10 miles.

Meanwhile John Davies and Jim Heathfield were doing battle with a string of Blackheath men a little further back. Both of our boys lost ground on the dangerous stretches with a sensible "safety first" policy but made it up in the last mile or so of even going; John, in particular, gaining several places.
Jim Heathfield took over from Collis on the second stage for the 'D' team with Bhatia running for the 'A', Shippen for the 'C' and Conway for the 'E'.
Don MacLean, now running more like his old self, finished second in the two mile event to Hugh Foord with a time of 9m.33.8s: other places:- K. Miller 11th(10m.3s.), J.
Gerry LeRoy won a sparkling 440 running in the out-side lane, and the ever versatile Jimmy Heathfield returned to the distance over which he was winning 12 years ago, to win the quarter in 54.6 secs.
In the 220 Dave was again our only entrant, but Jimmy Heathfield filled the breach, and although he failed to qualify was by no means outclassed.
Jim Heathfield ran his fastest half of the season finishing 3rd in 2:02.2, while John Ware finished 2nd, 3rd and 5th in the shot, discus and Javelin events.
The ever-consistent Jim Heathfield secured third place in the half with a time of 2:03.4 in a blanket finish, while Dave Ansell did an eye-opening 10.7 sec dash, in the 'B' event.
Jim Heathfield could not hold this place under heavy pressure and dropped back to sixth and handed over to Clive Shippen forty seven seconds in arrears.

Eric was followed in by Jim Heathfield, who is finding it very difficult to do any serious training now that he has changed his job. It was very pleasing to see 'new boy' Norman Stairs in his first distance race for us, running so well.
Eric Gebbett and Jim Heathfield represented the "A" and "B" teams. Eric held a forward position thro'out and his tenth position was only 19 secs behind the second man.
Jim Heathfield put in some useful running to take the handicap from Jim Rimmer ( a man to watch) who was a good second. Handicap Result: 1.J.Heathfield 26:13, 2.J.Rimmer 26:21, 3.D.Hurd 26:38
Thank your President (Ironware) and his Lady (Ladies' clothes), Dave and Win in comparable departments, Bill Lucas, Jimmy Heathfield and Ben Lullam (with tape measure) on the natty gents stall.

Jim Heathfield and Gordon Biscoe get a quote for "The Belgravian" from sage John Davies. Tom Carter admires Marcello Bizio's kingfisher and white ensemble.

We are not absolutely certain of the year but it was probably 1955, one of the years when Charlie Walker, (4) at the back of the pack became Club Champion over the distance. Behind Charlie Manning can be seen a youthful Jim Heathfield. Can anyone put names to the other faces in the picture?
